method.label: Write an equation for the remaining mean

annotationRationale: The mean relates each sum to its number of entries, producing a one-variable modeling equation solved by expanding parentheses.
sourceMethod: Follows the official remaining-mean equation with k removed entries, adding the intermediate algebra needed to obtain k=7.

review.mathCheck: The original sum is 900, so \(900-6k=66(20-k)\), yielding \(60k=420\) and \(k=7\), choice D. This leaves 13 entries totaling 858, whose mean is 66; the count and denominator are valid.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Attached AMC 12A solution #5 uses precisely this remaining-sum and remaining-count equation. The candidate gives an originally worded, faithful adaptation with enough intermediate algebra to reconstruct the solution.
review.annotationCheck: Mean and one-variable modeling are appropriately assessed. Expanding and solving the parenthesized equation is suitable supporting knowledge; weighted mean is not needed.
